From 49b32ddb87a3a109afecea89e55d70f73956b8bc Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Oliver Upton <oupton@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:59:00 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: arm64: nv: Fix handling of XN[0] when !FEAT_XNX

XN has already been extracted from its bitfield position so using
FIELD_PREP() on the mask that clears XN[0] is completely broken, having
the effect of unconditionally granting execute permissions...

Fix the obvious mistake by manipulating the right bit.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d93febe2ed2e ("KVM: arm64: nv: Forward FEAT_XNX permissions to the shadow stage-2")
Reviewed-by: Wei-Lin Chang <weilin.chang@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Oliver Upton <oupton@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260602165901.52800-2-oupton@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Marc Zyngier <maz@kernel.org>

index dc2957662ff2..cdf3e8422ea1 100644

2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a bug in the handling of XN (Execute-Never) permissions for nested virtualization on ARM64 (KVM). The error occurs when the system does not support the FEAT_XNX extension. In that case, the code incorrectly attempts to clear the lower XN bit using `FIELD_PREP()` on an already extracted value, which results in unconditionally granting execute permissions instead of properly masking the bit.

### Modifications per File

**File**: `arch/arm64/include/asm/kvm_nested.h`

- **Function `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el0`** (line 135):  
  Changed `xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);`  
  to `xn &= 0b10;`

- **Function `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1`** (line 151):  
  Changed `xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);`  
  to `xn &= 0b10;`

### Relationships

Both changes address the identical mistake in two closely related functions that determine whether execution is allowed at EL0 and EL1 respectively. The fix corrects the bitwise masking operation from an incorrect use of `FIELD_PREP` (which expects a raw value to be encoded into a bitfield mask) to a simple AND with the binary mask `0b10` (which isolates bit 1, i.e., XN[1]) on the already extracted 2-bit XN value.

Here is the root cause:
The code used FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10) to mask the extracted XN value, but FIELD_PREP shifts the value into the original bitfield position, whereas the variable xn already contains the extracted 2-bit value. This results in incorrect masking, effectively clearing the wrong bits and unconditionally granting execute permissions when FEAT_XNX is not supported.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);</text>
Reason:
FIELD_PREP shifts the value 0b10 to the original bitfield position, but `xn` already contains the extracted 2-bit value (0-3). The AND operation with the shifted mask then clears both XN bits unconditionally, granting execute permissions when FEAT_XNX is not supported.

Directly masking with `0b10` (binary 2) keeps the higher bit (XN[1]) and clears the lower bit (XN[0]), correctly respecting the intended behavior without the unintended FIELD_PREP shift.
